judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematical claims all hold. I recomputed every item independently: sqrt(64)=8, 0.24=24/100=6/25, sqrt(20)=4.4721...->4.47, sqrt(225)=15, 3.1 < 16/5 = 3.2 < sqrt(11)=3.3166..., 63/99=7/11, sqrt(40)=6.3245...->6.32, sqrt(3)=1.73205... > 1.73, sqrt(25/36)=5/6, sqrt(12)*sqrt(3)=sqrt(36)=6; and all eight study-guide boxes (sqrt(81)=9, sqrt(169)=13, sqrt(28)->5.29, sqrt(55)->7.42, 0.125=1/8, 0.27repeating=27/99=3/11, and both orderings). The worksheet does print exactly 10 problems across 4 pages. Where the judge is wrong is instruction_following 4/4. The prompt says 'clearly label any genuinely open response for manual review'; verify.json declares zero manual entries, gate_log.txt reports no manual flags, and final_response.md states outright 'nothing is flagged manual'. Yet problem 6(a) ('Explain why a decimal that repeats forever can still be rational'), problem 8 ('Explain in one sentence what 1.73 really is'), problem 3(c) and problem 10(b) are all open written responses - and answer_key.tex problem 10 even prints grader-judgment language, '(Accept any answer that identifies the claim as false and points at this product as the reason.)', which is the definition of a manual item. Separately, problems 3(a) and 7(a) ask 'between which two consecutive whole numbers' (4 and 5; 6 and 7) and problem 2 asks the student to fill a four-cell table row; verify.json covers one value per problem, so those machine-checkable responses are unbound.

strengths_to_preserve: The perfect-square table (n = 1..15 with n^2 beneath) is printed inside the directions and is the stated decision procedure for every root problem - problems 1, 3, 4, 7, 9 and 10 all resolve by looking a radicand up in that one row, so the 'model connected to notation' requirement is met by a device the student actually uses rather than decoration.

Problem 10 (sqrt(12) * sqrt(3) = sqrt(36) = 6) is a well-chosen closer: a single counterexample that disproves 'the product of two irrational numbers is always irrational', which is the misconception the rest of the sheet sets up. Keep this item.

The two declared traps (halving the radicand: 10 for sqrt(20), 20 for sqrt(40)) are machine-proved distinguishable from the correct values and print in the key's 'Common wrong answers' block, so a wrong paper names its own error.

root_causes.description: The contract has no way to say 'this part of the problem is a written explanation', so a problem that mixes a computable value with an explanation is recorded as fully machine-verified. Every open response on this sheet was silently absorbed into the one numeric entry for its problem.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 8 asks 'Explain in one sentence what 1.73 really is'; verify.json id 8 is a compare entry with expected '>' and no manual companion.

worksheet.pdf problem 10(b) asks a one-sentence justification; answer_key.tex problem 10 prints '(Accept any answer that identifies the claim as false ...)' - grader judgment - while verify.json id 10 is a single eval expecting 6.
gate_log.txt gate summary shows verify-ws PASS with no MANUAL, and final_response.md asserts 'nothing is flagged manual'.

root_causes.description: Multi-part problems are verified at one slot. Nothing in the pipeline relates the number of responses a problem asks for to the number of verify entries carrying its id, so parts (a) and (b) of a three-part item can be entirely unchecked while the build reports full coverage.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 3 has parts (a) bracket the root, (b) classify, (c) round; verify.json id 3 has one approx entry (4.47).
worksheet.pdf problem 7 repeats the same three-part shape; verify.json id 7 has one approx entry (6.32).
worksheet.pdf problem 2 prints a four-column table row (decimal, fraction as read aloud, lowest terms, rational?); verify.json id 2 verifies only 6/25, leaving 24/100 unchecked.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt sympifies string expected values and falls back to '---' when sympify raises. A relational answer ('>' / '<' / '=') can never sympify, so a verified answer prints in the bank as the same em-dash used for 'manual, see solution'.
evidence: verify.json id 8 is {'type': 'compare', 'order': 'relation', 'expected': '>'} and verify.py:1608-1622 supports exactly that form.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '8. ---' while the key body boxes 'sqrt(3) > 1.73'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt: the str branch returns '---' on SympifyError.

improvements.title: Declare the four written explanations on the irrational-numbers sheet as manual items
improvements.proposed_change: Require a companion {'type': 'manual'} entry, carrying the same problem id, whenever a problem's printed statement asks the student to explain, justify, describe or name something. Add a build lint that scans worksheet.tex problem bodies for those verbs and fails when the id has no manual entry. For this case that means manual companions on ids 3, 6, 8 and 10, and a final_response.md that reports 'N machine-verified, 4 manual' instead of 'nothing is flagged manual'.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ with a fixture problem whose statement contains an open-response verb ("explain", "name the error", "describe", "circle") and whose verify JSON has no matching manual entry, and assert the build reports an unflagged open response. It fails today (the fixture builds green with exit 0) and passes after the lint lands.
improvements.expected_impact: The teacher learns which items need reading rather than grading, and the delivery message stops overstating machine coverage. Judged as the second-largest systemic cluster across the run (36 cases).
improvements.risk: A keyword lint will fire on problems that merely use the word 'explain' inside a hint. Keep the lint scoped to the imperative sentence that owns an answer slot, and allow an explicit '"manual": false' acknowledgement to silence a false positive.

improvements.title: Cover the bracketing parts of problems 3 and 7 and the table cells of problem 2
improvements.proposed_change: Have the verify JSON declare, per problem, how many responses the sheet asks for, and require one entry per response. Here: add compare/eval entries for '4 < sqrt(20) < 5' and '6 < sqrt(40) < 7' (ids 3 and 7) and an eval entry for the 'fraction as read aloud' cell 24/100 (id 2). Fail the build when declared slots exceed entries for an id.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ that loads a fixture worksheet whose problem prints N distinct requested responses and a verify JSON covering fewer of them, and assert the build fails with a slot-coverage error. It fails today (no such check exists, so the fixture builds green) and passes once the answer-slot declaration is enforced.
improvements.expected_impact: Every value a student writes on this sheet becomes bound to a recomputed value; the largest systemic cluster in the run (61 cases) closes.
improvements.risk: Authors may pad slot counts to satisfy the gate. Mitigate by counting slots from the rendered answer lines and enumerated parts rather than trusting a hand-typed number.

improvements.title: Quick Answers prints an em-dash for problem 8's verified relation '>'
improvements.proposed_change: In scripts/render_quick_answers.py, special-case the answer shapes verify.py already supports but sympy.sympify cannot parse: render a relational expected ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=') as its math-mode symbol, and render an empty solution list as 'no solution'. Reserve '---' for genuinely manual-only ids.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/test_render_quick_answers.py with two cases: a compare entry of order "relation" with expected ">", and a system entry with expected [] (no solution). Assert the rendered bank lines read "$>$" and "no solution" rather than "---". Both assertions fail against the current _fmt/render_entry and pass after the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading column stops hiding verified answers behind the same em-dash it uses for 'see solution', on every sheet that contains a comparison or a special-case system.
improvements.risk: Very low; the change is additive and fixture-locked.

case_summary: A mathematically flawless 10-problem concept packet on rational versus irrational numbers: every worksheet answer, every study-guide box and both declared traps recompute correctly, the perfect-square table is a real working model rather than decoration, and problem 10's sqrt(12)*sqrt(3)=6 counterexample is an excellent closer. The ACCEPT verdict is right on the mathematics. What the judge did not check is the prompt's second sentence: four problems ask for written explanations and none is declared manual, while problems 2, 3 and 7 print more responses than verify.json covers. The answer key answers all of them correctly - the gap is in the verification contract, not the content. One cosmetic renderer defect: the verified relation '>' for problem 8 prints as '---' in the Quick Answers bank because render_quick_answers._fmt cannot sympify a comparison operator.
